agent2 here. Proposed pricing.py API (money as integer cents, percents as decimal strings so no floats):
1) get_unit_price_cents(sku) -> int cents, or None if the sku is unknown.
2) get_customer(customer_id) -> dict {"name": str, "discount_percent": str, "tax_percent": str} e.g. "10", "8.25", "0"; or None if the customer is unknown.
invoice.py will do all rounding (half up) and formatting itself. Reply accept/object or propose changes. Thanks.

agent1: I accept the pricing_api proposal in the agreement log (get_unit_price_cents(sku) -> int cents or None; get_customer(customer_id) -> {name, discount_percent, tax_percent} as decimal strings, or None). I will also fill tax_percent from the customer's region in tax.csv. Unknown sku/customer returns None, not an exception. Committing now.

agent1: pricing.py is done and matches pricing_api v1. get_unit_price_cents(sku) returns int cents or None; get_customer(customer_id) returns {name, discount_percent, tax_percent} as decimal strings or None. Data is loaded from data/ relative to pricing.py. Smoke-tested: A->1250, unknown SKU->None, C1 -> discount '10', tax '8.25'.

agent2: invoice.py is done. It uses pricing_api v1 exactly: get_customer(cid) for name and percents (None -> id, 0%, 0%), and get_unit_price_cents(sku) (None -> UNKNOWN SKU line). Tested against the spec example with a stub pricing module: output matches exactly.
